questions.statement: It is 7:00 in the morning. Mateo sees his teacher. What does he say?
questions.context: Son las 7:00 de la mañana en un colegio de Bucaramanga y Mateo entra al salón donde está su profesora.

options.feedback: Correct. "Good morning" is the greeting we use from the time we wake up until 12 noon, and 7:00 is in the morning.
Incorrect. "Good night" is said at night when we go to bed or leave, not at 7:00 in the morning.
Incorrect. "Good afternoon" is used after 12 noon, and 7:00 a.m. is still the morning.
Incorrect. "Goodbye" is a farewell for when you leave, but Mateo is arriving, so he needs a greeting.

questions.explanation: En inglés el saludo cambia según la hora. Desde que nos levantamos hasta las 12 del mediodía decimos "Good morning" (buenos días). Como Mateo llega a las 7:00 a.m., el saludo correcto es "Good morning!".
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which word do you say when you leave?
questions.context: Al terminar la clase en una escuela de Pereira, los niños se despiden de sus compañeros antes de irse a casa.

options.feedback: Incorrect. "Hello" is a greeting for when you arrive or meet someone, not for when you go away.
Incorrect. "Hi" is an informal way to say hello when you meet someone, so it starts a conversation instead of ending it.
Incorrect. "Good morning" greets people in the morning when you arrive; it does not mean you are leaving.
Correct. "Goodbye" is the farewell word that means you are leaving, so it is the word for the end of a meeting.

questions.explanation: Hay palabras para llegar (saludos) y palabras para irse (despedidas). "Hello", "Hi" y "Good morning" son saludos. "Goodbye" significa adiós y se dice cuando nos vamos, por eso es la respuesta correcta.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: Ana y Luis se encuentran en el recreo de su colegio en Cartagena y Ana le pregunta cómo está.

options.feedback: Correct. "How are you?" asks how you feel, and "I'm fine, thank you" answers with how Luis feels.
Incorrect. "I'm Luis" gives his name, which answers "What's your name?", not a question about how he feels.
Incorrect. "I'm eight years old" tells his age, which answers "How old are you?", not "How are you?".
Incorrect. "Good night" is a farewell for the night and does not tell Ana how Luis feels.

questions.explanation: La pregunta "How are you?" significa "¿Cómo estás?". Por eso la respuesta debe decir cómo se siente la persona: "I'm fine, thank you" (estoy bien, gracias). No hay que confundirla con "How old are you?", que pregunta la edad.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete: "Hello, my name is Sara. Nice to ______ you."
questions.context: Sara es una niña nueva en un colegio de Medellín y se presenta ante su compañero de puesto el primer día de clases.

options.feedback: Incorrect. "Make" means to build or create something, and the fixed phrase for a first meeting does not use it.
Correct. The phrase "Nice to meet you" is what we say when we see a person for the first time.
Incorrect. "Eat" is the action of having food, so "Nice to eat you" has no sense in a greeting.
Incorrect. "Sleep" is the action of resting at night, and it does not form a polite phrase for meeting someone.

questions.explanation: Cuando conocemos a alguien por primera vez decimos "Nice to meet you" (mucho gusto en conocerte). El verbo "meet" significa conocer o encontrarse con alguien. Los otros verbos ("make", "eat", "sleep") no forman esa expresión.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Read: "Pedro comes home from school at 3:00 p.m. He sees his grandmother in the kitchen."
What does Pedro say?
questions.context: Pedro vive en Tunja y llega a su casa después del colegio; su abuela lo espera en la cocina.

options.feedback: Incorrect. "Good night" belongs to the night or bedtime, and 3:00 p.m. is in the middle of the day.
Correct. "Good afternoon" greets people after 12 noon, and Pedro arrives at 3:00 p.m.
Incorrect. "Good morning" is used before 12 noon, but the text says Pedro arrives at 3:00 p.m.
Incorrect. "Goodbye" is said when you leave, but Pedro is arriving home and needs a greeting.

questions.explanation: Hay que leer la hora en el texto: "3:00 p.m." La sigla "p.m." indica la tarde. Después de las 12 del mediodía el saludo es "Good afternoon" (buenas tardes). Además Pedro llega, no se va, así que no sirve "Goodbye".
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Tom: "Bye, Mia! See you tomorrow."
Mia: "________"
questions.context: Tom y Mia salen del colegio en Cali y cada uno toma un camino distinto para volver a casa.

options.feedback: Incorrect. "Good morning" is a greeting for arriving in the morning, but Tom is saying goodbye.
Incorrect. "Nice to meet you" is for the first time you know someone, and Tom and Mia are already friends.
Correct. Tom says a farewell, so Mia answers with another farewell: "Bye" and "See you" both mean they are leaving.
Incorrect. "I'm fine, thanks" answers "How are you?", a question Tom never asks in this dialog.

questions.explanation: Tom se despide con "Bye" y "See you tomorrow" (nos vemos mañana). Lo natural es responder también con una despedida: "Bye, Tom! See you!". Las otras opciones son saludos o respuestas a otras preguntas.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Read: "Camila meets a new girl at school. The girl says: 'Hi! I'm Valeria.'"
What is the best answer for Camila?
questions.context: En un colegio de Barranquilla, Camila conoce a una niña que acaba de llegar de otra ciudad.

options.feedback: Incorrect. "Goodbye" closes a conversation, but Valeria is just starting one by saying hi.
Incorrect. "Good night" is for bedtime or leaving at night, and the girls are at school during the day.
Incorrect. Valeria did not ask "How are you?", she gave her name, so this answer does not match.

options.text: Hi, Valeria! I'm Camila. Nice to meet you.
options.feedback: Correct. Camila greets back with "Hi", gives her own name, and says "Nice to meet you" because it is their first meeting.

questions.explanation: Valeria saluda y dice su nombre. La mejor respuesta hace lo mismo: saluda ("Hi, Valeria!"), dice el propio nombre ("I'm Camila") y, como es la primera vez que se conocen, agrega "Nice to meet you" (mucho gusto).
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: La profesora de inglés de un colegio de Villavicencio escribe cuatro diálogos en el tablero y pide escoger el que está bien.

options.feedback: Incorrect. The first person speaks at night and the second answers with a morning greeting, so the times do not match.
Incorrect. "How are you?" asks how someone feels, and "My name is Juan" only gives a name.

options.text: "How are you?" - "I'm fine, thanks. And you?"
options.feedback: Correct. The answer tells how the person feels and asks back with "And you?", a polite and complete reply.
Incorrect. "See you" points to a future meeting, so "yesterday", a day in the past, does not fit, and it does not answer "Nice to meet you".

questions.explanation: Un diálogo correcto tiene una respuesta que encaja con lo primero que se dice. A "How are you?" (¿cómo estás?) se responde con el estado de ánimo: "I'm fine, thanks" y se puede devolver la pregunta con "And you?" (¿y tú?).
questions.subject: ingles
